concept.name: Secondary test
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (ST) in which price revisits the area of a climax to test the supply/demand balance there. In accumulation, a successful secondary test shows significantly diminished volume and spread as price approaches the selling-climax low, confirming that supply is drying up.
concept.intuition: The market dips back toward the panic low to see if any frightened sellers are left; if hardly anyone sells this time, the bottom is more likely real.
concept.mechanics: After a selling climax (accumulation) or buying climax (distribution), price returns toward the climax level; the analyst compares volume and spread with the climax. Diminished selling near the climax low confirms support, while an ST that breaks materially below the climax low warns of new lows or prolonged consolidation. Multiple secondary tests are common and occur throughout the range.
concept.failure_modes: A 'successful' low-volume test can still be followed by a breakdown if the broader market deteriorates, and judging whether volume is 'significantly diminished' is subjective.
concept.misconceptions: A secondary test does not have to hold exactly at the climax level, and one successful test does not complete a base; several STs over months are typical.
concept.example: Two weeks after a panic low at 90, the stock sinks to 91 on one-third of the earlier volume and closes mid-range; the analyst logs a successful secondary test confirming Phase A.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
